candidate_core_topology.topology: two independently regulated four-ASIC series strings

regulator.candidate_vout_derivation: 4 series ASICs × ESP-Miner BM1373 per-chip voltage options 1.00-1.25 V

power_sizing.classification: derived: 280 W measured wall anchor × provisional 0.90 wall-to-board factor
power_sizing.conservative_model_rule: for regulator-current sizing, treat the entire stated board-power envelope as if delivered by VCORE; this overstates VCORE current because controller/fans/auxiliary loads are excluded from the subtraction

why_this_replaces_four_two_chip_domains: Four chips at the current ESP-Miner BM1373 voltage options require 4.0-5.0 V per series domain, inside the TPS546D24S PMBus output range up to 5.5 V.
Two TPS546D24S devices stacked per domain provide 80 A datasheet capability, leaving materially more current headroom than one 40 A device on each two-chip domain.
Only four TPS546D24S devices are required for eight ASICs instead of the prior eight-device candidate.

The topology is directionally consistent with Gamma Hex using multi-ASIC series voltage domains and a stacked TPS546D24S regulator, but BM1373 operation with four ASICs per series domain remains unproven.
hard_validation_gates: BM1373 four-ASIC series-domain startup and steady-state voltage sharing must be proven on hardware.
Cross-domain UART/clock/reset level shifting must be validated specifically for four series ASICs per domain.
TPS546D24S compensation, inductors, switching frequency, current limit and thermal solution must be recalculated for the actual selected VCORE/load.
PMBus telemetry must be checked against independent current/voltage instrumentation before it is trusted for protection.
No fabrication release while downstream placement, copper, thermal and protection models still reflect the superseded four-domain architecture.

facts_used: BOM contains two TPS546D24S for two ASICs
